design_status: Committed fixed study specification; designed stress tests, not a registered or representative benchmark. No seed search or outcome-based selection.
noise: Independent uniform(-sqrt(3)*sd, sqrt(3)*sd) record errors before rounding; the same standard draws are paired across scenarios.
observation_rounding: Decimal(str(value)), ROUND_HALF_UP to 0.01 yield percentage points; no clipping, rejection, or seed selection.
target: Per-concentration mean yield; concentrations receive equal weight for every model.
validation: Leave one entire concentration out; baselines are refitted from only the three remaining group means. Quadratic folds come from the production scientific result.
alias_design: The quartic and low-noise quadratic agree exactly at all four tested concentrations. With paired errors their sealed observations are identical. This is a deliberately adversarial identifiability example, not a claim about citrus chemistry.
aggregation: Pooled RMSE is sqrt(mean(squared residuals)) over all available trial-point pairs. Trial RMSE min/median/max describe these fixed simulations, not confidence intervals. Failures are counted separately; an unavailable quadratic candidate is not a failed prediction model.
limitations: Synthetic numerical investigation only; no real experiments, students, or efficacy evidence.
Four concentrations and five synthetic independent records per concentration do not establish physical independence in classroom data.
Twelve fixed seeds are a small reproducibility panel, not a representative benchmark or statistical certification.
LOCO target is a noisy held-out group mean; grid target is the unrounded noiseless generating function. Their errors answer different questions.
Endpoint LOCO folds extrapolate beyond their training range; interior folds interpolate.
Three-point quadratic folds are saturated. Small CV error cannot establish an unseen optimum or distinguish observationally aliased functions.
No model, hyperparameter, or experiment is selected from the held-out grid or these study results.
The production candidate rule remains conservative and is assessed separately from prediction accuracy.
